statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-113351: XML_ParserReset zeroed the direct byte count without offsetting tracked heap allocations, so after a large document a reused parser could fail with XML_ERROR_NO_MEMORY; the CVE record lists libexpat 2.7.2 through 2.9.0 as affected (https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-113351). Upstream fixed it in Expat 2.10.0 (libexpat pull request #1431, https://github.com/libexpat/libexpat/pull/1431; release notes https://github.com/libexpat/libexpat/blob/R_2_10_0/expat/Changes). Alpine's aports expat APKBUILD lists the fix under 2.10.0-r0 (https://gitlab.alpinelinux.org/alpine/aports/-/blob/3.23-stable/main/expat/APKBUILD). The DHI Alpine 3.23 repository publishes expat builds 2.7.3-r0, 2.7.4-r0, 2.7.5-r0, 2.8.1-r0, 2.8.2-r0, 2.8.3-r0, 2.8.3-r1, 2.8.4-r0, 2.8.5-r0, 2.8.5-r1, 2.9.0-r1 and 2.10.0-r1, built from aports. We checked the libexpat package of every one of these builds for x86_64 and aarch64 against the index checksum: libexpat.so.1 reports Expat 2.7.3 to 2.9.0 in the builds before 2.10.0-r1 and Expat 2.10.0 in 2.10.0-r1. We also ran the upstream reset test from that pull request against each of these libraries on both architectures (parse a document of about 70 MiB, call XML_ParserReset, then parse '<hello/>'): every build before 2.10.0-r1 fails the second parse with XML_ERROR_NO_MEMORY, and 2.10.0-r1 parses it. The expat-static package ships libexpat.a from the same source release, and the xmlwf program in the expat package links libexpat.so.1 dynamically. The range ends at 2.10.0-r1, the first published build with the fix.
